title: Sections of an etale sheaf of sets over a strictly henselian local open are its stalk
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U\subseteq T$ an open subscheme with an isomorphism $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] for a strictly henselian local ring $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point] whose image is the point $u\in U$ corresponding to $\mathfrak m$. The inclusion $j:U\to T$ is etale, so $(U,\bar t)$ (with $\bar t$ regarded as a morphism to $U$) is a pointed etale neighbourhood of $\bar t$ [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods]. Then for every sheaf of sets $G$ on $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] the germ map $G(U)\to G_{\bar t}$, $a\mapsto$ the germ of $a$ at $(U,\bar t)$ (stalk of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]), is bijective. (For $U=T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ this is Stacks 03QO for sheaves of sets; its abelian version is lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-sections-stalk.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 03QO (lemma-vanishing-etale-cohomology-strictly-henselian), 'In fact we have Gamma(S, F) = F_sbar for any sheaf of sets F', and its proof (an etale neighbourhood (W, wbar) receives a section through Theorem Tag 04GG/Theorem 'theorem-henselian' A = R x A'; hence the identity neighbourhood is cofinal); here run inside T for the open U (the etale neighbourhood W of tbar in T is replaced by W x_T U, an etale neighbourhood of tbar over U)

proof.text: Represent a germ in the stalk by a section over an object (V, vbar) of N_tbar, with structure morphism f: V -> T. Let v be the image of vbar and let u = f(v), which lies in U. Apply the affine-shrink lemma with the open W = f^{-1}(U) containing v. It gives an open immersion j: Spec A -> V through v, with f o j etale. Since j(Spec A) is contained in W, f o j factors through the open immersion U = Spec R -> T (def-weil-open-immersion); write the factor as Spec(phi): Spec A -> Spec R for the induced ring map phi: R -> A (def-weil-affine-spectrum). The factored morphism is etale because the local rings of the open U and T agree, so the etale condition is unchanged (def-weil-etale-morphism). If q is the prime of A corresponding to the lifted marked point, then phi^{-1}(q) = m because f(v) = u and u corresponds to m.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03QO and the affine-neighbourhood reduction in its proof

proof.text: The residue extension at q is finite separable by the etale-algebra residue-field lemma, and the residue field kappa of R is separably closed, so the extension is an isomorphism by finite separable triviality. Via the open immersion j, the residue map f^#: kappa(u) -> kappa(v) is this isomorphism. The henselian root-lifting criterion and the etale retraction lemma then give an R-algebra retraction tau: A -> R with tau^{-1}(m) = q. Let sigma be j o Spec(tau), viewed as a map U = Spec R -> V. It is a T-morphism because f o sigma is the inclusion U -> T: on rings this is tau o phi = id_R. Moreover sigma(u) = v, since tau^{-1}(m) = q. Let alpha: kappa(u) -> Omega and beta: kappa(v) -> Omega be the field maps of tbar and vbar. The equality f o vbar = tbar gives beta o f^# = alpha; the equality f o sigma = inclusion gives sigma^# o f^# = id, so sigma^# = (f^#)^{-1}. Thus the field map of sigma o tbar is alpha o sigma^# = beta o f^# o (f^#)^{-1} = beta, and both geometric points have image v. By def-weil-geometric-point and def-weil-residue-field, sigma o tbar = vbar. Hence sigma is a morphism (U, tbar) -> (V, vbar) in N_tbar (def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods).

source.place: Lemma Tag 03QO proof, using Theorem Tag 04GG

proof.text: The category N_tbar of pointed etale neighbourhoods is cofiltered by lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered. The object (U, tbar) receives a morphism from it to every object by step 2. Its singleton full subcategory has only the identity endomorphism: a T-morphism h: U -> U satisfies j o h = j, and the open immersion j is injective on points and an isomorphism onto its image, hence h = id. Therefore lem-weil-pbc-colimit-initial-full-subcategory (1) applies. With the colimit of the resulting constant diagram (G(U), id) computed by lem-weil-pbc-colimit-constant-connected-diagram, the canonical map is the coprojection iota_(U, tbar), namely the germ map. Hence G(U) -> G_tbar is bijective.

tool_uses.why: Affine pointed-neighbourhood shrinking is a generic etale-site tool used to represent an arbitrary germ.
The finite separability of residue extensions for etale morphisms is used to trivialize the marked residue field.
The separably closed residue field turns the finite separable residue extension into an isomorphism; this generic field lemma is in another unit.
The henselian simple-root lifting criterion supplies the lift used in the etale retraction.
The lifted root is packaged as the retraction of the etale algebra, a generic henselian tool from another unit.
Cofilteredness of N_tbar is required by the hypotheses of the initial-full-subcategory colimit lemma.
Cofinality of the singleton identity-neighbourhood subcategory is the categorical reduction of the stalk colimit.
The reduced singleton colimit is computed as a constant connected diagram.
